# Autonoma Environment Factory SDK

> This package implements the Autonoma Environment Factory: a single backend endpoint that provisions isolated test data before an end-to-end test run and tears it down afterward. You author named scenarios in your own code with `defineScenario` (or your language's equivalent); the SDK owns HMAC authentication, the signed teardown token, and expiry. These docs are bundled inside the installed package so a coding agent reads the API that matches this exact version, instead of relying on training data.

If you are setting up the endpoint, read `implement.md` and follow it step by step. The other files are reference.

## Reading order

1. overview.md - What the Environment Factory is, the three actions (discover/up/down), scenarios as ordinary code, what `up` returns, and the two secrets. Start here.
2. implement.md - Step-by-step setup for this language: install, author scenarios, wire the handler, return real credentials from `up`, and validate. This is the doc to follow when integrating.
3. scenarios.md - How to author scenarios: `name`/`description`/`up`/`down`, the `{ auth, teardown }` return, seeding unique values, the `unique*` helpers, and how to choose journey-based scenario names. Language-agnostic.
4. factories.md - Legacy SDK v1 factory compatibility for migrations. Not v2 authoring guidance and not wired to the v2 protocol.
5. protocol.md - The HTTP wire protocol: authentication, the three actions, the teardown token, the safety model, and every error code. Language-agnostic. Reach for this when debugging.
6. validation.md - How to dry-run a scenario in this language before deploying.
